thread:
Sam: Hey @people-ops — quick q about a job-share situation. Ava and Ben share a 1.0 role. Ava is planning ~12w paid parental starting Jun 1. Ben wants to take ~6w earlier and then come back part-time. Do we treat parental leave per person or per role? Also who handles benefits/proration and is there a standard handoff expectation?

Elena (People Ops): Short answer: leave is per eligible employee, not per role. If both Ava and Ben meet eligibility, each gets our paid parental benefit separately. :white_check_mark:

Elena (People Ops): A few follow-ups: 1) We do need written leave requests in the HR portal for each person. 2) Part-time returns change FTE which can affect PTO accruals and some ancillary benefits — payroll + benefits team will confirm exact proration. 3) We usually expect a short overlap (1–2w) for handoff where feasible.

Sam: awesome. Are there limits on overlapping paid leaves for the same headcount? manager is worried about coverage and budget for backfill.

Rachael (Benefits): We don't claw back parental pay because two people share an FTE — benefit eligibility is individual-based. Health insurance employer contributions continue during paid leave per policy. For part-time return: employee must submit a change-of-status within 30 days so we can update benefit deductions/proration.

Rachael (Benefits): If they drop below benefits-eligibility hours after return, they'll get a notice and options (COBRA where applicable).

Sean (Payroll): From payroll side: mark time off with code "PARENTAL_PAY" for paid weeks. For part-time returns we'll change the employee's FTE on the next payroll cutoff (please provide the effective date). Any FTE change requires a new compensation record and may affect prorated bonuses/stock vesting schedule admin — work with People Ops for approvals.

Sean (Payroll): For temporary contractor funding to cover coverage gaps, create a "backfill request" via the finance intake form with the UTCs and duration. Payroll won't auto-fund contractors — we need budget signoff.

hr-bot: Hi! Link to policy: https://redwood.example.company/hr/parental-leave — submit leave requests and attach medical/birth/adoption docs there. This channel cannot view attachments.

Sam: Great, thanks. Can we get a short checklist of what Ava/Ben need to file and by when?

Elena (People Ops): Yes. Please have both employees submit the portal requests at least 30 days before start if possible. If it's short-notice, file ASAP and include expected dates.

Elena (People Ops): Checklist (paste to employee):
```
- Submit leave request in HR portal (select "Parental Leave")
- Attach birth/adoption paperwork or physician letter (if available)
- Indicate planned return date and whether returning part-time (include requested FTE)
- If requesting contractor/backfill, have manager submit finance intake form with dates and budget owner
- Confirm PTO usage plan (e.g., use PTO to cover top-ups) and sign PTO payout/hold options
- Schedule 1:1 with People Ops to review benefits changes
```

Sam: Perfect. One more Q — if Ben returns part-time (0.6 FTE), do we keep his slot open for recruiting a temp for remaining 0.4? Or hire a contractor for full time?

Elena (People Ops): Typical pattern: hire a short-term contractor for the fractional gap when speed is needed, or a fixed-term contractor for predictable multi-month coverage. If you want a headcount hire, submit a req and note it's a temporary/term role. Finance will evaluate cost between contractor vs fixed-term.

Ben: Thanks everyone — I'll put my portal request in today and indicate a 0.6 return. Also happy to overlap 1 week with Ava to hand off.

Ava: Thx — I'll file mine this afternoon and plan for a 2-week handoff window.

Sam: Going to start the finance intake for contractor coverage now. @Elena can you confirm who to loop in for approval?

Elena (People Ops): Loop @Rachael for benefits headcount impact, @Sean for payroll coding, and @finance-approvals (alias) for budget. I'll join the intake review. If anyone wants, we can set a 20-min quick sync to walk through the portal UI and approvals.

Sam: Thanks — let's do the sync. :calendar:

Elena (People Ops): I'll DM avail times and create a short agenda.

Sam: Appreciate it.

(End of thread)
